    The sponge construction (EasyCrypt proof/Sponge.ec) — EC-fidelity port #

    Ported on the strict tactics: Sponge_is_StdSponge (EC l. 99); the whole theory HybridIRO (EC l. 256–1909; l. 1188–1282, the modules BlockSpongeTrans and BlockGen, are the first port's); Sponge_Raise_BlockSponge_f (EC l. 1922), which was the second tactic experiment and is described below; and the final section with conclusion (EC l. 1913–2163).

    Translation:

    • the modules are the first port's (section FirstPort below); a procedure takes its parameters as one tuple there, so a statement names them at the triple (StdSponge(P).f (x) ~ …, HybridIROLazy.f (xs, n) ~ …);
    • the theory HybridIRO is a namespace; its module variables HybridIROLazy.mp, HybridIROEager.mp and those of the local clone ERO are global_vars;
    • a local clone's variables are fresh for a declared module in EC; here the restriction names them (-ERO.RO.m, -ERO.FRO.m).

    Gap list (batch-fix later, see TRANSFER_SKILL.md §1.6):

    • GAP 1 (closed 2026-11-17): a procedure of a module of one clone's module type, read at another clone's (LowerDist(Dist) hands BlockSponge's primitive to the bit sponge's Dist), is opened by equiv_proc as EC's proc does.
    • GAP 2: inside the library's RO.sample the callee is the library's RO.get itself, not the procedure of the module ERO.RO, so EC's inline ERO.RO.get does not name it: by index.
    • GAP 3 (closed 2026-11-21): after a call whose result is discarded, the strict auto did not read through the discarding write (Setter.throwaway_set is now among the reads' lemmas).
    • GAP 4: the abstract call asks all of HYBRID_IRO's procedures, where EC's {HI.f} restricts D to f: one more goal, for init. (HybridIROLazy.init, .f are declared as the module type's procedures of HybridIROLazy, the form in which a call of an oracle names them; the first port's own procedures are equal to them only by a rewrite.)
    • GAP 5 (closed 2026-11-22): equiv_conseq H left its two implications when the goal's conditions are not literally H's; it closes them now when they are logic alone, as EC's.
    • GAP 6 (closed 2026-11-21): the strict auto ran out of recursion depth (in its closing simp_all) on the body of a one-sided loop whose invariant reads the other memory; a closing attempt that hits a runtime limit now leaves the goal as EC's auto does.
    • GAP 7 (closed 2026-11-21): the exit goal of a one-sided loop framed what the postcondition reads, not what the invariant reads (xs{1} in next_block_split_BlockSpongeTrans, added to EC's conseq there); its frame now has both.
    • GAP 8: transitivity N (P₁ ==> Q₁) (P₂ ==> Q₂) on procedures is the rule prhlProc_trans_ec, not a tactic: the second judgment is its own lemma, and the side conditions are over the parameter tuples (hypotheses restated by replace before use).
    • GAP 9 (closed 2026-11-18): BlockGen_loop_direct is EC's bypr proof, no longer the first port's restated by a rewrite.
    • GAP 10: after a loop, the guard's read of a local and the invariant's read of it can be different atoms for omega (equal by rfl): le_antisymm on the two hypotheses instead.
    • GAP 11: ={bs} in a condition of equiv_trans is not resolved when the two sides of the goal have a bs of different types, although the middle program's is the left one's: §(localVarLens "bs" (List Bool)){1} = §(localVarLens "bs" (List Bool)){2}.
    • call (_ : ={HybridIROEager.mp}) on the concrete fill_in needs its footprint, which EC reads off the code: fvP_HybridIROEager_fill_in, fvP_BIRO_IRO_fill_in (@[fp_bound]). The callee's goal (EC: if=> //; wp; rnd; auto) is then closed by the tactic.
    • GAP 12 (closed 2026-11-21): the strict auto and equiv_skip ran out of recursion depth on a goal whose conditions have bs{1} = take n1 bs{2} next to ={bs}; EC's skip; smt(take_size) since the closers' runtime limits are caught (2026-11-21).
    • GAP 13 (closed 2026-11-22): sim did not pass an inlined call that copies its parameters and has a loop (inline HybridIROEagerTrans.next_block; sim): the loops' callee is named through the port's alias on one side, and sim's pairs of locals now compare such callees by definition.
    • A middle program of transitivity is over the variables the goal mentions, not the whole memory: where EC's condition names a variable that neither side reads any more (n{2} = n1 %/ r), the conjunct is dropped; an inlined parameter keeps its name when the caller no longer reads one of that name (EC's n0 is n).
    • equiv_conseq H on procedures states post without the precondition, where EC keeps it: equiv_conseq_pre H (Logic/ECConseqHoare.lean) where the proof needs it. exists* on a procedure judgment reads the declared parameter names (§x{1} for HybridIROEager.f's xs). A side goal about parameters and results is over their tuple types: introduce them at the plain types (rintro ⟨xs, (n : ℤ)⟩ … (r₁ : List Bool)), restate the hypotheses by replace, and change the goal, before rw or omega.
    • EC's alias{2} 1 with w is not needed: the sampled block is the inlined callee's local r (two locals bs, r of different types on the two sides are read as §(localVarLens "bs" (List Bool)){1}).
    • A statement that names HIRO(…).f's parameters (xs, n) as EC does gets a warning: the module type HYBRID_IRO declares them (x, n).
    • GAP 14 (exception E2): EC's module type SIMULATOR lists the oracles of each procedure (init { }, f {F.f}, fi {F.f}); declare module knows them only for a functor with one procedure. The final section states them as a hypothesis (BlockSim_rep, the first port's SIMULATOR.Representable). From it: BlockSim_init_call for EC's call (_ : true) on BlockSim(F).init, and EC's proc (I) on BlockSim(F).f, .fi by equiv_proc (I) (Logic/ECProcInv.lean) with the first port's rules SIMULATOR.call_f, call_fi tagged @[proc_inv]. EC's swap past BlockSim(F).init has no footprint to check (the oracle list is known for the procedure's behaviour, not for its code): the call's invariant says what the swap would (equiv_call (_ : ={glob Dist, glob BlockSim} ∧ §HybridIROLazy.mp{2} = FMap.empty), the rule SIMULATOR.call_init).
    • GAP 15: sim finds no equality set for a call of Dist whose oracles are the same on both sides when the precondition's equalities are a glob region and a variable (={glob Dist, glob BlockSim, HybridIROLazy.mp}): the call with EC's set (equiv_call (_ : ={glob BlockSim} ∧ §mp{1} = §mp{2})), the simulator's oracles by equiv_proc (I) and sim, the concrete one by a judgment ={x, mp} ==> ={res, mp} (sim) under equiv_conseq_frame.
    • EC's call (_ : P ==> Q). proc (I)=> //. on the declared Dist is one step, equiv_call (_ : ={glob BlockSim} ∧ I) (the ={…} ∧ without parentheses); the implication that EC proves next (progress; apply lazy_invar0) is then in the last goal, with the code before the call.
    • EC's conseq H where the goal keeps a glob that H does not mention: equiv_conseq_frame H (Logic/ECProcInv.lean), which frames what the procedures do not write and closes the two implications when they are trivial; a section's module that H's procedures do not name is given (RaiseHybridIRO_HybridIROEager_RaiseFun_BlockIRO_f BlockSim).
    • The frames need the footprints of the first port's concrete modules (@[fp_bound] lemmas before the final section, each by fp_module). Two traps: omit [BlockSponge.Params] on such a lemma makes fp_module fail on a procedure that calls another one (the first port's unfolding lemma takes the instance), and a bound stated after include R takes R as an argument and is not found.

    Sponge_Raise_BlockSponge_f in EC's form — the second tactic experiment #

    A procedure-level equivalence with two-sided loops, EC's inline M.f, seq n m : P, rcondt{i}, case, call (_ : ={glob Perm}) on a concrete module and auto, over the old port's declarations (section FirstPort below). It drove stmt_inline (M.f) (Logic/ECInline.lean), EC's equiv_seq positions (Logic/ECSeq.lean), equiv_auto, equiv_call (_ : ={glob P}) on a concrete callee, and the closers of hoare_auto/equiv_auto.

    Deviations, all from the old declarations or the closers:

    • the statement: (bs, n) as one parameter x, named at the triple; the old views as coercions;
    • positions: one more statement on each side (bs, n <- x), a skip where rcondt left the branch, RaiseFun's xs <- z0 taken by stmt_wp; EC's swap{2} [3..5] -2, swap{2} 1 1 and seq 0 1 are not needed (the inlined code is already in that order);
    • EC's smt/progress/rewrite closers: simp_all with the blocks2bits lemmas.

    Declarations of the first port #

    Definitions and plain lemmas of the first port of this file (2026-10/11) that the proofs below use; its program-logic proofs are gone.

    The first port's translation notes (some mention declarations that went with its proofs):

    • clone include Indifferentiability with type p <- block * capacity, type f_in <- bool list * int, type f_out <- bool list rename … "Indif" as "Experiment" … is the abbreviations below.
    • clone import IRO as BIRO with type from <- bool list, type to <- bool, op valid <- valid_toplevel, op dto <- dbool is the namespace BIRO; EasyCrypt's unqualified IRO is BIRO.IRO.
    • Procedures whose EasyCrypt parameters (bs, n) are the module type's single parameter take that pair and name its components, as in BlockSponge. HYBRID_IRO.f is not a functionality: it keeps its two parameters.
    • LowerDist(D, F) = D(RaiseFun(F)) is used as LowerDist(Dist) : BlockSponge.DISTINGUISHER: D is a Lean parameter, and the alias is wrapped in a call (exception E5). RaiseSim(S, F) = S(LowerFun(F)) is the composite Module.comp S LowerFun.
    • The abstract theory HybridIRO is the namespace HybridIRO. Its modules' variables (HybridIROLazy.mp, HybridIROEager.mp) are lens parameters, as for every generic theory.
    • Variables of local clones (ERO in HybridIRO, HIRO in the last section) are lens parameters of the local declarations that mention them, with hypotheses that they are fresh for the section's modules; the non-local results do not mention them (exception E6).
    • EasyCrypt's proc distinguish() is a RO_Distinguisher, whose procedure takes unit; here RODist's distinguish takes that Unit parameter.

                                        Module.app StdSponge P = Module.pair init (Module.app f P)

                                        @[simp]: applying StdSponge to a tuple of its single parameter P — the record of its procedures StdSponge.init, StdSponge.f, each applied to the parameters it uses.

                                                                                                                                                                      theorem GaudisCrypt.SHA3.Sponge.HybridIRO.HIRO.init.apply_simp [SLCommon.Params] [BlockSponge.Params] (RO : ERO.RO_T) :
                                                                                                                                                                      Module.app init RO = Module.proc (procedure.instantiate (EC.PROM.FullRO.RO_T.init (List Common.block × ℤ) Bool RO).procedure)

                                                                                                                                                                      @[simp]: applying HIRO.init to the parameters proc init uses (RO) is Module.proc (HIRO.init.procedure.instantiate …) — the procedure with its holes filled by the callees they were made from, each written as it was in the body (with the arguments in place of the module parameters) and turned into a Procedure by Module.Proc.procedure.

                                                                                                                                                                      noncomputable def GaudisCrypt.SHA3.Sponge.HybridIRO.HIRO.init.procedure :
                                                                                                                                                                      proctype () → Unit uses (() → Unit)

                                                                                                                                                                      The body of proc init of module HIRO, as a procedure of its own: the one call it makes to a module parameter (RO) is its single hole.

                                                                                                                                                                      A hole stands for a call whose callee is not known here — a module parameter is supplied only when the module is applied — so the body is a ProcedureWithHoles, to be instantiated (see HIRO.init.procedure.apply_simp) rather than run. Use HIRO.init for this procedure as a module.

                                                                                                                                                                        theorem GaudisCrypt.SHA3.Sponge.HybridIRO.HIRO.apply_simp [SLCommon.Params] [BlockSponge.Params] (RO : ERO.RO_T) :
                                                                                                                                                                        Module.app HIRO RO = HYBRID_IRO.mk { init := Module.app init RO, f := Module.app f RO }

                                                                                                                                                                        @[simp]: applying HIRO to a tuple of its single parameter RO — the record of its procedures HIRO.init, HIRO.f, each applied to the parameters it uses.

                                                                                                                                                                        This is the lemma that unfolds a module use: simp rewrites with it, then with the field lemmas of the module type (N.f.mk_simp) to get at the one procedure the goal is about, and then with HIRO.init.apply_simp, HIRO.f.apply_simp to fill that procedure's holes.

                                                                                                                                                                        theorem GaudisCrypt.SHA3.Sponge.HybridIRO.HIRO.init.procedure.apply_simp [SLCommon.Params] [BlockSponge.Params] (holeArgs✝ : (HoleSigs.cons (procsig () → Unit) HoleSigs.empty).Instantiation) :
                                                                                                                                                                        procedure.instantiate holeArgs✝ = proc () : Unit { call (holeArgs✝.lookup HoleIndex.zero) (); return () }

                                                                                                                                                                        Instantiating the holes of HIRO.init.procedure with a tuple holeArgs of procedures: the body of proc init as written, with each hole call replaced by the matching holeArgs.lookup (HoleIndex.zero being the first hole the body declared). True by rfl.

                                                                                                                                                                        Deliberately not @[simp], unlike the other apply_simp lemmas: its right-hand side is the whole body written out, so letting it fire on its own would turn any goal mentioning an instantiated procedure into that body. Inlining a procedure is a step to ask for by name (simp [HIRO.init.procedure.apply_simp]).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      {-IRO, -BlockSponge.BIRO.IRO}anddeclare module Dist <: DISTINGUISHER {-Perm, -BlockSim, -IRO, -BlockSponge.BIRO.IRO}`

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      local clone HybridIRO as HIRO: the clone is local, so its module variables HIRO.HybridIROLazy.mp, HIRO.HybridIROEager.mp are the lens parameters HIRO_Lazy_mp, HIRO_Eager_mp of the local declarations that mention them, fresh by hypothesis (HIRO_fresh, exception E6). HIRO.X is HybridIRO.X at these lenses.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        A hole stands for a call whose callee is not known here — a module parameter is supplied only when the module is applied — so the body is a ProcedureWithHoles, to be instantiated (see HybridIRODist.distinguish.procedure.apply_simp) rather than run. Use HybridIRODist.distinguish for this procedure as a module.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Footprints of the concrete modules of the final section #

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    EC reads a concrete module's globals off its code; the frame rules ask fp_le for a bound on a concrete callee, which it has for the modules it can read and otherwise takes from the lemmas stated here (@[fp_bound]), each proved by fp_module. They are what the frames of call H, conseq H and proc (I) below are found from. Not EC lemmas.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |Pr[ (Sponge.RealIndif Sponge.Sponge Common.Perm Dist) () @ &m : §res = true ] - Pr[ (Sponge.IdealIndif Sponge.BIRO.IRO.asF (Sponge.RaiseSim BlockSim) Dist) () @ &m : §res = true ]| = |Pr[ (BlockSponge.RealIndif BlockSponge.Sponge Common.Perm (Sponge.LowerDist Dist)) () @ &m : §res = true ] - Pr[ (BlockSponge.IdealIndif BlockSponge.BIRO.IRO.asF BlockSim (Sponge.LowerDist Dist)) () @ &m : §res = true ]|

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    EC's lemma conclu &m : |Pr[RealIndif(Sponge, Perm, Dist).main() @ &m : res] - Pr[IdealIndif(IRO, RaiseSim(BlockSim), Dist).main() @ &m : res]| = |Pr[BlockSponge.RealIndif(BlockSponge.Sponge, Perm, LowerDist(Dist)).main() @ &m : res] - Pr[BlockSponge.IdealIndif(BlockSponge.BIRO.IRO, BlockSim, LowerDist(Dist)).main() @ &m : res]|.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Conclusion (EC l. 2148–2163) #

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    theorem GaudisCrypt.SHA3.Pilot.Sponge.conclusion [SLCommon.Params] [BlockSponge.Params] (BlockSim : BlockSponge.SIMULATOR) [Module.Declared BlockSim (Sponge.BIRO.IRO.mp.footprint ⊔ BlockSponge.BIRO.IRO.mp.footprint ⊔ HybridIRO.HybridIROLazy.mp.footprint ⊔ HybridIRO.HybridIROEager.mp.footprint ⊔ HybridIRO.ERO.RO.m.footprint ⊔ HybridIRO.ERO.FRO.m.footprint)] {R : Footprint VariableAssignment} [Module.ECGlob BlockSim R] [R.Restricted (Sponge.BIRO.IRO.mp.footprint ⊔ BlockSponge.BIRO.IRO.mp.footprint ⊔ HybridIRO.HybridIROLazy.mp.footprint ⊔ HybridIRO.HybridIROEager.mp.footprint ⊔ HybridIRO.ERO.RO.m.footprint ⊔ HybridIRO.ERO.FRO.m.footprint)] (Dist : Sponge.DISTINGUISHER) [Module.Declared Dist (Common.Perm.m.footprint ⊔ Common.Perm.mi.footprint ⊔ R ⊔ Sponge.BIRO.IRO.mp.footprint ⊔ BlockSponge.BIRO.IRO.mp.footprint ⊔ HybridIRO.HybridIROLazy.mp.footprint ⊔ HybridIRO.HybridIROEager.mp.footprint ⊔ HybridIRO.ERO.RO.m.footprint ⊔ HybridIRO.ERO.FRO.m.footprint)] (BlockSim_rep : Indifferentiability.SIMULATOR.Representable (Common.block × Common.capacity) (List Common.block × ℤ) (List Common.block) BlockSim) (m : VariableAssignment) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |Pr[ (Sponge.RealIndif Sponge.Sponge Common.Perm Dist) () @ &m : §res = true ] - Pr[ (Sponge.IdealIndif Sponge.BIRO.IRO.asF (Sponge.RaiseSim BlockSim) Dist) () @ &m : §res = true ]| = |Pr[ (BlockSponge.RealIndif BlockSponge.Sponge Common.Perm (Sponge.LowerDist Dist)) () @ &m : §res = true ] - Pr[ (BlockSponge.IdealIndif BlockSponge.BIRO.IRO.asF BlockSim (Sponge.LowerDist Dist)) () @ &m : §res = true ]|

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    EC's lemma conclusion (BlockSim <: BlockSponge.SIMULATOR{-IRO, -BlockSponge.BIRO.IRO}) (Dist <: DISTINGUISHER{-Perm, -BlockSim, -IRO, -BlockSponge.BIRO.IRO}) &m : |Pr[RealIndif(Sponge, Perm, Dist).main() @ &m : res] - Pr[IdealIndif(IRO, RaiseSim(BlockSim), Dist).main() @ &m : res]| = |Pr[BlockSponge.RealIndif(BlockSponge.Sponge, Perm, LowerDist(Dist)).main() @ &m : res] - Pr[BlockSponge.IdealIndif(BlockSponge.BIRO.IRO, BlockSim, LowerDist(Dist)).main() @ &m : res]|.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The restrictions also name the variables of the theory HybridIRO and of its local clone ERO (fresh in EC), Dist's restriction against BlockSim is the region form (with glob R, E14), and the oracle lists of EC's module type SIMULATOR are the hypothesis BlockSim_rep (E2).
